title: Dutch Baby Pancake with Berries, Lemon and Icing Sugar
summary: A smooth egg-rich batter is poured into foaming butter in a hot cast-iron pan and baked until puffed, then finished with lemon, berries and icing sugar.
equipment: 26 cm cast-iron or heavy ovenproof frying pan

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
lemon, juice and a wedge to serve

steps.title: Heat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 220 °C (200 °C fan) with a shelf in the middle. A very hot oven makes the batter puff.

steps.title: Blend the batter
steps.text: Blend the eggs, flour, milk, sugar, vanilla, nutmeg and salt for about 30 seconds until very smooth, or whisk hard by hand. Room-temperature eggs and milk help it rise.

steps.title: Heat the pan
steps.text: Put the butter in the pan and heat it in the oven for 3-5 minutes, until melted and foaming but not brown.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Take the pan out, swirl the butter round the sides, pour in the batter at once and return it to the oven. Bake for 20 minutes without opening the door, until puffed high and deep golden. Lower the oven to 150 °C (130 °C fan) and bake 5 minutes more so the centre sets fully.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: It will sink a little, which is normal. Squeeze over the lemon juice, add the berries, dust with icing sugar and cut into 4 wedges at the table. Remember the handle is very hot.

tips: Opening the oven door early is the commonest mistake; the cold air makes it collapse before it sets.
The pan and butter must be hot when the batter goes in.
A heavy cast-iron pan gives the crispest edges.
Keep an oven glove on the handle as a reminder that it is hot.
storage: Best eaten straight from the oven; it does not keep well. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
